# Limits

<!-- codeflow-derived limits begin: generated by codeflow from the binary; do not edit between the markers. Regenerate with CODEFLOW_REGENERATE_LOOKUPS=1 cargo test -p codeflow-cli derived_lookup -->

Every limit CodeFlow applies: timeouts, retries, counts, sizes, waits, parallel numbers and word limits, each with its key, default, bounds and class. The binary generates this page from its limits registry, so a limit a maintainer adds appears here without further work. To choose which models CodeFlow uses, see [model and harness upgrades](model-upgrades.md).

Set a limit by adding its key to the file its section names. An absent key keeps the default. A value of the wrong type or outside the bounds refuses, naming the key and its bounds.

- **Operational** limits tune how long or how much work may take. The bounds are only what correctness needs, and a large value is never refused.
- **Security** limits keep a control fail-closed. You can tighten one to its floor at any time, and raise it to its ceiling. The ceiling leaves a buffer: the guard deadline always stays inside the guard hook timeout.
- **Guidance** values are only reported. CodeFlow warns, and never refuses, queues, waits or lowers what you set.

## Set in `.codeflow/policy.json`

| Key | Default | Bounds | Class | What it limits | Why |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `git.remote_query_timeout_seconds` | `30` seconds | a whole number of seconds, at least 1; no ceiling beyond what the number can hold | operational | remote query wait per attempt | GitHub answered the pre-push default-branch lookup in 11.3 s and 11.6 s on 2026-11-03, over the earlier fixed 10 s; 30 s leaves room above that while a silent destination still refuses |
| `git.remote_query_attempts` | `3` attempts | a whole number of attempts, at least 1; no ceiling beyond what the number can hold | operational | remote query attempts | the earlier lookup made one attempt and two retries; only a timeout is retried, so a refusal stays final |
| `git.remote_fetch_timeout_seconds` | `120` seconds | a whole number of seconds, at least 1; no ceiling beyond what the number can hold | operational | remote fetch wait | the earlier fixed fetch wait; a fetch carries objects, so it gets longer than a lookup |
| `limits.guard_deadline_seconds` | `20` seconds | a whole number of seconds from 5 to 24 | security | guard deadline | a 10 s buffer under the 30 s guard hook timeout, so the guard's own refusal reaches the harness before the harness stops waiting and lets the call through in Codex and Grok (TSK-1082); the ceiling keeps 6 s for a slow host's refusal write and process exit, and the floor stays above a loaded host's slowest guard |
| `limits.guard_pr_lookup_wait_seconds` | `5` seconds | a whole number of seconds from 1 to 7 | security | guard pull request lookup wait | fits after one guard remote lookup with a 5 s buffer under the 20 s guard deadline; no answer in time is doubt, and the guard blocks on doubt |
| `coord.check_interval_seconds` | `600` seconds | a whole number of seconds, at least 1; no ceiling beyond what the number can hold | operational | coordination check interval | the check cadence the coordination loop ships with; ten minutes keeps a watcher current without spending the forge rate limit |
| `coord.heartbeat_timeout_seconds` | `1800` seconds | a whole number of seconds, at least 1; no ceiling beyond what the number can hold | operational | coordination heartbeat timeout | three missed check intervals: a session that is working reports well inside it |
| `limits.coord_max_recheck_seconds` | `86400` seconds | a whole number of seconds, at least 1; no ceiling beyond what the number can hold | operational | longest coordination recheck | a recheck further out than a day would hide a waiting item |

| `limits.ledger_refusal_lock_wait_seconds` | `1` seconds | a whole number of seconds, at least 1; no ceiling beyond what the number can hold | operational | ledger refusal lock wait | How long a hook or guard waits for another writer's lock on this ledger before it gives up on the record and keeps its verdict. |
| `limits.doctor_version_probe_timeout_seconds` | `5` seconds | a whole number of seconds, at least 1; no ceiling beyond what the number can hold | operational | doctor version probe timeout | the wait for a tool to print its version |
| `limits.doctor_codex_load_timeout_seconds` | `20` seconds | a whole number of seconds, at least 1; no ceiling beyond what the number can hold | operational | doctor codex load timeout | How long one Codex command may take before it counts as not run. |
| `limits.doctor_gh_timeout_seconds` | `15` seconds | a whole number of seconds, at least 1; no ceiling beyond what the number can hold | operational | doctor gh timeout | Each `gh` call is bounded, so an unreachable host cannot hang doctor. |
| `limits.runner_heartbeat_interval_seconds` | `300` seconds | a whole number of seconds, at least 1; no ceiling beyond what the number can hold | operational | runner heartbeat interval | how often a quiet target reports that it is still running |
| `limits.portal_git_timeout_seconds` | `30` seconds | a whole number of seconds, at least 1; no ceiling beyond what the number can hold | operational | portal git timeout | the wait for one git read in the portal check |
| `limits.work_start_review_lookup_timeout_seconds` | `15` seconds | a whole number of seconds, at least 1; no ceiling beyond what the number can hold | operational | work start review lookup timeout | Maximum provider wait for the review evidence of one predecessor pin. |
| `limits.guard_brace_word_limit` | `64` words | a whole number of words from 16 to 64 | security | guard brace word limit | the most words one brace expansion yields before the guard refuses; the ceiling is the default because the expansion cost multiplies |
| `limits.guard_brace_depth_limit` | `256` levels | a whole number of levels from 8 to 256 | security | guard brace depth limit | brace groups one word may nest before the guard refuses; it bounds recursion, so the ceiling is the default |
| `limits.guard_brace_word_bytes` | `4096` bytes | a whole number of bytes from 1024 to 4096 | security | guard brace word | the longest word brace expansion reads; the longest path the supported systems open, and the nested scan costs the square of the length, so the ceiling is the default |
| `limits.guard_brace_char_limit` | `10` characters | a whole number of characters from 6 to 12 | security | guard brace char limit | the `{`, `}` and `,` characters a word may hold for the guard to read its braces; each may be quoted, so readings double per character and the ceiling stays near the default |
| `limits.guard_glob_entry_limit` | `4096` entries | a whole number of entries from 256 to 65536 | security | guard glob entry limit | directory entries one glob expansion reads before it stops; a monorepo with very wide folders can raise it, and the ceiling matches the secret walk so a guard still answers before its deadline |
| `limits.guard_secret_entry_limit` | `65536` entries | a whole number of entries from 4096 to 262144 | security | guard secret entry limit | directory entries a secret-path walk reads before it refuses; a large monorepo can raise it, and the ceiling keeps a cold walk on a slow disk inside the guard deadline |
| `limits.guard_run_dir_limit` | `64` entries | a whole number of entries from 8 to 256 | security | guard run dir limit | directories one line can move to before the guard reports the directory as unknown; a generated script with many `cd` steps can raise it |
| `limits.guard_sed_script_bytes` | `16777216` bytes | a whole number of bytes from 65536 to 16777216 | security | guard sed script | the largest `sed -f` script the guard reads; a larger one is refused, and the ceiling is the default because the guard holds the script in memory |
| `limits.guard_target_candidates` | `8` entries | a whole number of entries from 2 to 16 | security | guard target candidates | directory candidates for one git target before it counts as unknown; each candidate costs a repository read on a slow host |
| `limits.edit_guard_walk_limit` | `4096` entries | a whole number of entries from 64 to 4096 | security | edit guard walk limit | entries of a protected directory walked before the walk stands for the whole directory; past it the guard treats the directory as protected, and the ceiling is the default |
| `limits.guard_git_config_bytes` | `4194304` bytes | a whole number of bytes from 1048576 to 67108864 | security | guard git config | the most git configuration the guard reads before it refuses; a host with very large includes can raise it, and the ceiling bounds what one guard holds in memory |
| `limits.guard_dir_set_limit` | `64` entries | a whole number of entries from 8 to 64 | security | guard dir set limit | directories a directory set lists before it reads as unknown; the ceiling is the default because every later step is read against each one |
| `limits.guard_root_read_limit` | `4096` entries | a whole number of entries from 64 to 16384 | security | guard root read limit | directories read below one root before the root counts as reaching a class file; a monorepo can raise it, and the ceiling keeps a slow disk inside the guard deadline |
| `limits.remote_answer_bytes` | `16777216` bytes | a whole number of bytes from 1048576 to 67108864 | security | remote answer | how much a remote may say; a repository with very many refs can raise it, and the ceiling bounds what a hostile remote can make the process hold |
| `limits.glob_path_bytes` | `32000` bytes | a whole number of bytes from 4096 to 32000 | security | glob path | the longest path the matcher scans against one pattern; it sits under the Windows path limit so every host gives the same refusal past it (TSK-1258), so the ceiling is the default |
| `limits.sandbox_settings_read_bytes` | `16777216` bytes | a whole number of bytes, at least 1024; no ceiling beyond what the number can hold | operational | sandbox settings read | the most bytes read from one settings file by `codeflow doctor`, which only reports |
| `limits.doctor_probe_timeout_seconds` | `5` seconds | a whole number of seconds, at least 1; no ceiling beyond what the number can hold | operational | doctor probe timeout | how long `codeflow doctor` waits for one runner probe; a probe past it is reported and blocks nothing |
| `limits.guard_git_read_seconds` | `3` seconds | a whole number of seconds from 1 to 5 | security | guard git read wait | one local git read inside a guard; no answer in time is doubt, and the guard blocks on doubt; a slow disk can raise it, and the ceiling keeps several reads inside the guard deadline |

## Set in the test configuration

| Key | Default | Bounds | Class | What it limits | Why |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `timeout_seconds` | `600` seconds | a whole number of seconds, at least 1; no ceiling beyond what the number can hold | operational | target timeout | ten minutes suits a typical target; the ceiling is only what the deadline arithmetic can hold |
| `stall_timeout_seconds` | `300` seconds | a whole number of seconds, at least 1; no ceiling beyond what the number can hold | operational | target stall timeout | five quiet minutes with no output or CPU is a stall (TSK-1278); the ceiling is only what the deadline arithmetic can hold |
| `cleanup_grace_seconds` | `5` seconds | a whole number of seconds from 1 to 3600 | operational | target cleanup grace | the bound on termination, reaping, watcher shutdown and pipe draining after termination starts (TSK-1278); an hour keeps every deadline sum far inside `Instant` and `Duration` arithmetic |
| `execution.host_jobs` | `0` jobs | none; reported only | guidance | host job budget | omitted, the budget is computed from the logical cores and available memory |
| `execution.worker_budget` | `0` jobs | none; reported only | guidance | run worker budget | omitted, a run uses the host budget; set, it is used as set, even above the computed budget |

## Set in `.codeflow/ci-wait.json`

| Key | Default | Bounds | Class | What it limits | Why |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `timeout_minutes` | `30` minutes | a whole number of minutes, at least 1; no ceiling beyond what the number can hold | operational | hosted CI wait | a typical hosted run finishes inside half an hour; zero would fail the gate at once, and the ceiling is only what a duration in seconds can hold |
| `poll_interval_seconds` | `30` seconds | a whole number of seconds, at least 5; no ceiling beyond what the number can hold | operational | hosted CI poll interval | a shorter interval risks the forge rate limit, so the floor is what correctness needs; a longer one only reports later |

## Set in the present configuration

| Key | Default | Bounds | Class | What it limits | Why |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `closed_days` | `30` days | a whole number of days, at least 1; no ceiling beyond what the number can hold | operational | present closed retention days | the shipped present retention default |
| `max_closed_sessions` | `100` entries | a whole number of entries, at least 1; no ceiling beyond what the number can hold | operational | present closed sessions | the shipped present retention default |
| `max_project_bytes` | `524288000` bytes | a whole number of bytes, at least 1; no ceiling beyond what the number can hold | operational | present project state bytes | the shipped present retention default |

## Set on the command line

| Key | Default | Bounds | Class | What it limits | Why |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `execution.heavy_wait_seconds` | `0` seconds | none; reported only | guidance | wait for a host-exclusive target | heavy runs never wait for each other by default; set today by `codeflow test --wait-seconds`, and TSK-1279 brings back the configuration key |

## Not settable

| Key | Default | Bounds | Class | What it limits | Why |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| none | `30` seconds | fixed | security | guard hook timeout | written into each harness's hook file and read by the harness, not by CodeFlow; a guard answers in about 0.1 to 0.5 s on a loaded host, so 30 s leaves room for a cold start and a slow disk while bounding how long a stalled guard holds a session (TSK-1082) |
| none | `10` seconds | fixed | security | guard remote lookup wait | a guard waits this long only while it is still working out which policy applies, so no policy can set it; a 10 s buffer under the 20 s guard deadline for the guard's other work; `git fetch` removes the need to ask |
| none | `1` seconds | fixed | security | guard refusal write wait | a stderr pipe nobody reads must not hold the exit; the guard deadline's ceiling is sized around this exact second, so moving it would break the nesting under the hook timeout |
| none | `100` milliseconds | fixed | security | guard deadline poll | the deadline's own clock: a short tick so a refusal lands within a tenth of a second of the deadline, costing nothing a project would tune |
| none | `4` times | fixed | operational | heavy target timeout multiplier | about four times the supplied quiet coverage run (1713 s); a project sets the target's own `timeout_seconds` instead, and the largest accepted timeout is computed from this factor, so it cannot move on its own |
